meaning: Every finite list of natural-number primes has a prime outside the list
question: Can a bounded exact construction produce an independently checked outside-prime certificate, without claiming native verification of the universally quantified theorem?
domain: natural numbers, exact integers; not Real/f64
candidate: N = product(P) + 1; q is a prime divisor of N; N = q*k; q not in P
checker: Independent product reconstruction, finite input prime checks, exact factor equation, outside-list relation and exhaustive q-divisor checks; producer searches only to isqrt(N), checker tries all 2 <= d < q until refutation or budget
logical_assumptions: Every integer N >= 2 has a least divisor greater than one and that divisor is prime
A divisor of both M and M+1 divides 1
The arbitrary finite-list argument is a classical mathematical proof external to the current Adva proof checker
protected: Universe is a typed research predicate, not an implemented builtin
One finite extension does not certify all finite lists
q outside a list need not exceed its largest member
No fixed fuel covers all natural numbers
Zero and one remain distinct; divisibility uses integer witnesses, not a field quotient or native M1
residuals: Rust prime-certificate verifier is a proposed adapter, not implemented or run
Adva has no admitted natural-number quantified theorem checker for Universe(Prime)
No universal grammar, social-value or native free conclusion
